title: Mother's French songs and the Catholic church
summary: His mother could not play but sang French songs and sacred music and spoke almost no English; the family was Catholic and the society had a band for parades.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Anything else about your family? Did anyone else, your mother play anything?
My mother couldn't play her anything. But my mother could sing very good, but all French.
Yeah. Did she sing in any churches or any religious sacred music?
Well, she sung songs and she sang sacred music, too. But my mother sung mostly all French's numbers, French songs. Yeah. In other words, she couldn't speak 15 words in English.
French, very French. I knew it's a French name that you have. That's right. Were you raised to speak French when you were a boy?
Well, I did. I learned it mostly about her. Of course, my daddy could speak it, too. But not as pure French as my mother could speak French.
I wondered if you heard any church music in those days. Were you all... Did you belong to the Catholic Church or any other church?

Well, we all belonged to the Catholic. I've been to the Catholic. I'm still Catholic now. And they had a benevolent association. It's a society that used to play for the parade. The society is here. The society is over there. They used to play parade just like those people parading here.
